passages.provision_quote: A governmental entity may substantially burden a person's exercise of religion only if the governmental entity demonstrates that application of the burden to the person: (1) is in furtherance of a compelling governmental interest; and (2) is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest.
passages.note: Enrolled text of SB 101's general compelling-interest/least-restrictive-means standard, the provision Clere voted on.

passages.provision_quote: Prohibits a governmental entity from substantially burdening a person's exercise of religion, even if the burden results from a rule of general applicability, unless the governmental entity can demonstrate that the burden: (1) is in furtherance of a compelling governmental interest; and (2) is the least restrictive means of furthering the compelling governmental interest.
passages.note: Legislature's digest of SB 101; Clere is not among the listed authors, co-authors, or sponsors, only a voting House member.
House Roll Call 305, final passage of SB 101, records Clere's own vote.
passages.actor_quote: Brown, C Hale Niezgodski Stemler Clere Kersey Pelath Summers

rows.reasoning: Rep. Clere voted Nay on House Roll Call 305 for SB 101 (2015), Indiana's Religious Freedom Restoration Act, whose operative section lets a person assert a religious-burden claim against any governmental entity statute unless the government proves a compelling governmental interest and the least restrictive means -- the general faith-based-exemption mechanism rung 4 describes ('allow faith-based exemptions from laws that conflict with sincere religious beliefs'). A Nay vote on this single-subject bill rules out that broad exemption standard but does not establish which of rungs 1-3 he would support instead.
